tickets.summary: K-3401 non-drive-end bearing vibration rose from 2.1 to 4.6 mm/s in six weeks and had not plateaued, though below alarm; a trip of this sole gas export train would cut production within an hour.
tickets.recommended_action: Have a rotating equipment specialist diagnose the bearing and 1x sidebands; repair per findings, trend daily and confirm stable vibration below alarm. Obtain source-required attention today. Check current run state, vibration and spectrum.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The non-drive-end bearing vibration more than doubled over six weeks and had not plateaued, strongly indicating progression toward loss of reliable compressor operation. It was not yet at alarm; a trip or present function loss is not established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: If bearing-related failure trips this single gas export compressor train, there is no spare or workaround: the platform goes to recycle and production is cut within the hour. This is a severe operational consequence, not an observed trip.

tickets.summary: Possible PSV-1310 outlet weep—hissing and hydrocarbon smell below set pressure—raises concern for V-1201 overpressure protection; relief capability and current personnel exposure remain unverified.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect PSV/outlet; have the pressure-safety engineer assess controls and approve any indicated repair. Check impairment/deviation register. Verify set-pressure lift and seat tightness. Check hydrocarbon source and deck exposure. Check current state and repair history.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Audible hissing and a hydrocarbon smell at the outlet, while operating pressure is below set pressure, are advanced indications of possible passing. They do not establish that the PSV cannot relieve V-1201 overpressure; the source and present condition remain unverified.

impact_of_failure.rationale: If this nonredundant PSV loses its required relief function, V-1201 loses its stated overpressure protection, creating a credible severe safety consequence. The observation does not establish that this loss has occurred.

tickets.summary: FW-8102 missed its first weekly start; the second took ~8 s before rated pressure was reached, with batteries at 22.8 V at rest. Firewater-on-demand is impaired; FW-8101 later made 9.2 vs 11 barg with flow unmeasured, so backup capacity is unverified.
tickets.recommended_action: Firewater engineer: inspect starting system, repair faults found and approve disposition. Check impairment/deviation register. Load-test batteries; check starting air. Test FW-8101 flow/pressure vs criteria. Witness FW-8102 first-start, rated pressure and required flow.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is FW-8102 starting on demand to supply firewater. It failed the first weekly-test start, confirming loss of that function on that attempt. Starting on the second attempt and reaching rated discharge pressure do not erase the first failure or establish reliable starting.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure to start on demand degrades firewater protection. FW-8101 is the named N+1 partner, but its later test recorded 9.2 barg against 11 barg design without measuring flow. Its required delivery capacity cannot yet be credited or declared lost; the evidence does not establish that both pumps are unavailable.

tickets.summary: At window 2 by the low-point drain, wet insulation and scaling accompany 6.2 mm wall on the live 6-inch flowline, below the 7.4 mm minimum. Adjacent windows pass, but containment loss could release full-pressure hydrocarbons.
tickets.recommended_action: Refer to the integrity engineer for fitness and operating disposition; develop an approved repair for the sub-minimum wall. Map CUI extent and repeat UT. Confirm operating state and leak status. Check nearby personnel exposure. Confirm repair status; verify ≥7.4 mm and integrity.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is containment by the production flowline. A UT reading of 6.2 mm is below the 7.4 mm minimum at a wet, heavily scaled location, supporting advanced local damage. Adjacent windows are within tolerance, but containment loss has not been observed and the full extent is unknown.

impact_of_failure.rationale: If containment fails, this nonredundant production flowline could release hydrocarbons at full wellhead pressure. The credible severe consequence is supported, while the magnitude of personnel exposure remains unverified.

tickets.summary: FG-0455 failed to detect 50% LEL test gas twice. Both other 2oo3 heads passed then, preserving the compression module's tested gas-detection vote but leaving no margin for another head failure; restoration is unknown.
tickets.recommended_action: Instrument engineer to set interim controls and disposition; repair or replace the head according to diagnosis. Check impairment/deviation register. Verify head status; witness 50% LEL retest. Verify both other heads' current response. Inspect head gas path, optics and signal.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is this detector head's response to hydrocarbon test gas. It failed on both attempts, confirming loss of that head's required function; the other heads do not reduce its likelihood score.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of this head degrades hydrocarbon detection in the compression module. The other two heads responded at the test, leaving the 2oo3 group capable then but without margin for another head failure; their current status needs checking.

tickets.summary: The main hoist rope has 6 broken wires per lay versus a 10-wire discard limit at the maximum-radius drum-spooling section, with poor lubrication; hoist failure could injure personnel and halt supply-boat offloads within days.
tickets.recommended_action: Have the lifting inspector assess rope extent and lubricate the poor section; obtain lifting-authority repair and service disposition. Witness hoist test; verify rope against the lifting criterion. Recount wires; verify crane survey/service status. Check lift-area exposure and load paths.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is safe load hoisting by the main hoist rope. Six broken wires are below the stated discard criterion of ten, but poor lubrication supports limited degradation. The survey does not establish operational function loss or a progression rate.

impact_of_failure.rationale: If the hoist rope fails during a lift, a dropped load could seriously injure exposed personnel. Crane loss would also prevent supply-boat offloads and become a logistics problem within days; no redundant crane is listed. Personnel exposure and lift conditions remain unverified.

tickets.summary: On 6 June, P-3305 had its third low-pressure trip that month, with roughly ten days of intermittent manifold injection. Production continues, but inhibitor starvation risks delayed downstream steel corrosion; the diaphragm is only suspected.
tickets.recommended_action: Obtain corrosion engineer's operating/repair disposition; correct the diagnosed fault. Check impairment/deviation register. Confirm dose criterion; test current/repaired injection. Review gap logs and assess downstream steel. Inspect pump, discharge and diaphragm.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is P-3305 delivering corrosion inhibitor to the wellhead manifold. Three low-discharge-pressure trips and intermittent injection establish loss of reliable delivery; the diaphragm is only a suspected cause. Current restoration is unverified.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of inhibitor delivery does not stop production immediately, but can leave downstream carbon steel corroding within weeks, with delayed integrity consequences. No redundant pump is listed; downstream condition is unknown.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is structural support at the primary brace-to-node connection. impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of a primary cellar-deck support connection could have severe structural and personnel consequences. No redundant support is identified; supported loads and personnel exposure remain unspecified, so wider consequences cannot be asserted.

tickets.summary: HVAC-7201 achieved only 27 Pa against the refuge’s 50 Pa minimum despite rated fan speed, failing gas-exclusion pressurisation; a suspected damper or seal fault could expose mustering people to hydrocarbons.
tickets.recommended_action: Safety engineer to assess interim controls and authorize fault-based repair. Inspect damper closure and door seals. Check refuge impairment/deviation register. Verify current refuge protection controls. Retest refuge pressure against 50 Pa minimum.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is HVAC-7201 maintaining the required temporary-refuge envelope pressure. Its function test measured 27 Pa against a 50 Pa minimum, confirming loss of that function despite the fan running at rated speed. The damper and seal explanations remain suspected.

tickets.summary: On 10 June, ~12/60 north-quadrant deluge nozzles failed to deliver effective spray above two producing wellheads despite normal header readings; local fire coverage was impaired, and later valve reopening does not prove restoration.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect north branch/nozzles; clear or repair as found, with fire-protection engineer operating and repair disposition. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Map north nozzle/branch extent. Verify north valve alignment. Repeat full-flow test; confirm north coverage.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is delivery of effective deluge spray from the north-quadrant nozzles. The full-flow test confirmed loss of that function at some nozzles, although header pressure and flow were normal. Later reopening of a branch valve does not establish restored nozzle performance.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of local deluge delivery can leave two producing wellheads without effective spray coverage in an incident. Normal header readings do not establish coverage at the nozzles, and no redundant deluge arrangement is listed; the extent of coverage loss still needs checking.

tickets.summary: Port freefall lifeboat was declared unavailable after its notchy release needed excess force; class withheld certification pending overhaul. Evacuation capacity is reduced, but coverage of current POB is unknown.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect hydraulics; overhaul release gear under class surveyor oversight. Verify current POB against certified available evacuation capacity. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Verify availability and capability of LB-4101. Check status; witness retest; verify class certificate.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is LB-4102's availability to launch for evacuation. Its certificate was withheld and it was declared unavailable, confirming loss of that required operational function; the survey does not establish that physical launch is impossible.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of this craft reduces certified evacuation capacity and could leave personnel without sufficient capacity. LB-4101 is listed as N+1, but its capability and the capacity-versus-POB comparison are unverified, so neither adequate coverage nor an extreme shortfall is established.

tickets.summary: INST-2150 reads ~12% above backup and ~15% above sight glass, diverging for three weeks while controlling V-1201; the backup later flat-lined, leaving level control and high-level alarm reliability in doubt.
tickets.recommended_action: Instrument engineer: inspect duty loop and impulse path; correct proven faults and approve interim control/alarm disposition. Check impairment/deviation register. Compare both loops, sight glass and alarm. Check level history, setpoint and safeguards.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The duty transmitter's indication has diverged progressively from both the backup and sight glass while it supplies control. This strongly suggests worsening measurement reliability, but neither an acceptance limit nor a definitive reference check establishes complete loss of its required indication function.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of a reliable duty level signal could misdirect V-1201 interface-level control and degrade its high-level alarm. The backup's later flat-line report prevents crediting it as a capable alternative; actual level exposure and other independent safeguards remain unverified.

tickets.summary: V-1305's inlet deflector is partly detached after one bracket corroded through, threatening well-test separation; the shell and heads are sound, and the out-of-service vessel can be bypassed without production impact.
tickets.recommended_action: Plan next-shutdown inspection of all deflector brackets and attachment; repair as approved by the integrity engineer before well-test use. Verify deflector support and inlet-flow duty after repair.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: A corroded-through bracket and partly detached inlet deflector are meaningful precursors to loss of its inlet-flow function. Complete functional loss is unproven, and the separator is out of service.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of the deflector's inlet-flow function could interrupt well-test separation. The vessel is out of service and can be bypassed without production impact; its shell and heads are sound. Engineering acceptance is required before well-test use.

urgency.rationale: triage-policy-v5: ceil(0.7*I+0.3*L), L=5, I=4, base=5, final=5. tickets.summary: A dirty fuel-gas scrubber gauge weakens the local level cross-check. Transmitter control appears normal with no downstream carryover indications, but lost level assurance could expose turbines to liquid carryover.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect and clean the gauge glass using an approved isolation procedure; replace it if it remains obscured. Check gauge readability at operating level. Check transmitter control and downstream trends.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is readable local level indication from the gauge glass. It is degraded but described as hard to read, not unreadable; no progression or loss of level control is reported.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of the local reading would remove a level cross-check. Transmitter control appears normal and there are no downstream carryover indications, limiting the supported consequence; loss of level assurance still matters because the scrubber protects turbines from liquid carryover.

urgency.rationale: triage-policy-v5: ceil(0.7*I+0.3*L), L=4, I=5, base=5, final=5. tickets.summary: PSV-3420's corroded tag is illegible, but its March 2025 recertification is in date and the valve looks sound; relief loss is not observed. Failure to relieve compressor-discharge overpressure could expose the pressure boundary.
tickets.recommended_action: Replace the corroded tag under authorized PSV procedures; verify the new tag is legible and reflects the in-date certificate.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is this valve's compressor-discharge overpressure relief. Its tag is illegible, but the register shows in-date recertification, the valve looks physically sound, and the engineer reports it behaving itself. The documentation defect gives little indication of near-term relief-function loss.

impact_of_failure.rationale: If this valve fails to relieve compressor-discharge overpressure, a safety-critical protection layer with no stated redundancy is lost. That credible pressure-boundary hazard supports severe impact; the illegible tag does not reduce the consequence.

tickets.summary: FW-8101 started, but 9.2 barg versus 11 barg design with flow unmeasured leaves firewater delivery for fire control uncertain; pump wear or a test-line valve is suspected. FW-8102 earlier failed its first start, then succeeded; backup capability needs verification.
tickets.recommended_action: Firewater engineer to approve operating disposition and findings-based correction. Check deviation/impairment register. Witness duty flow/pressure now & post-fix vs approved criteria. Check FW-8102 start and current status. Inspect pump and test-line valves.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: FW-8101 started and ran correctly, but its test discharge pressure was 9.2 barg against an 11 barg design value. This is a meaningful delivery-capability concern, not proof of required-function loss: flow and the applicable acceptance criteria were not established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: If this pump cannot deliver required firewater, fire protection is degraded. FW-8102 is the identified partner, but its earlier first-start failure prevents assuming dependable backup; it subsequently ran at rated discharge pressure. The registry states that both pumps being unavailable would mean production shutdown, but their concurrent unavailability is not established.

tickets.summary: INST-2151's reported ~36-hour flat signal lost credible backup level indication; the duty leg had been drifting while controlling V-1201 and feeds its high-level alarm, leaving current protection status uncertain.
tickets.recommended_action: Instrument engineer assess operation; inspect impulse line/sensor, repair as found; retest backup against changing sight-glass level. Check impairment/deviation register. Verify duty accuracy, alarm links and status. Confirm current backup restoration.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The required function is credible independent backup interface-level indication. The reported approximately 36-hour flat line was explicitly judged not credible for this service, establishing loss of that function. A blocked impulse line and a failed sensor remain alternative suspected causes.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Losing the backup removes an independent level check. On June 11 the duty transmitter was increasingly discrepant while assigned to control, and it also feeds the high-level alarm. This supports material control and protection concern, but does not establish a failed alarm or the duty leg's current capability.

tickets.recommended_action: Restrict access below; secure or replace loose lagging and cladding as inspection indicates, then verify retention after correction. Check personnel access beneath cladding. Inspect fixings and confirm repair status.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is to retain the second-stage discharge-line cladding. It remained attached but was loose and flapping, with a dropped object expected if left. impact_of_failure.rationale: If cladding retention fails, the resulting dropped object presents a credible personnel-injury hazard. Exposure beneath it is unverified. The finding reports no process concern, so a compressor trip is not attributed to this defect.

tickets.summary: The north-quadrant deluge branch was found chained shut, interrupting wellhead-area water delivery for an unknown duration. It was reopened, but delivery is unverified; an earlier test separately found 12 of 60 nozzles with no or distorted spray.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect valve/nozzles; engineer to direct tagging and any repairs. Verify current protection control alignment. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Witness function test; close impairment only after pass. Check closure duration and nozzle coverage. Check wellhead personnel/fire exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is delivery through the north-quadrant deluge branch. Its chained-closed isolation valve prevented that delivery when found, confirming loss of the branch function. It was reopened immediately, but restored delivery has not been verified. The earlier nozzle-flow failure is a separate observed deficiency, not proof that the valve caused it.

impact_of_failure.rationale: If north-quadrant delivery fails during a wellhead fire, local deluge coverage is lost above two producing wellheads, creating severe fire and potential personnel exposure. No redundant deluge path is identified; the evidence does not establish total system loss or the magnitude of personnel exposure.

tickets.summary: Damp, rust-stained insulation at V-1201’s manway may conceal deterioration, but shell condition is unknown. Loss of its first-stage pressure boundary could release process contents and interrupt separation.
tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer assess exposed metal and approve operating/repair disposition; correct defects found and verify boundary to approved criteria. Check V-1201 deviation register. Expose manway; inspect/UT shell and pipework. Check personnel exposure at manway. Check current V-1201 repair/status.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is retention of first-stage pressure by the V-1201 shell. Damp insulation and rust staining are a meaningful precursor to concealed deterioration, but no shell wall loss, leak or near-term progression has been established. The vessel is described as thick-walled and historically trouble-free; the linked flowline finding does not establish a defect in this shell.

impact_of_failure.rationale: If the V-1201 pressure boundary fails, loss of first-stage containment could release process contents, interrupt separation and expose personnel. No redundant vessel is identified. Release magnitude and personnel exposure are unknown, so an extreme consequence is not assumed.
